analysis:
The only text change in this PR is documentation in docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The date bump at line 3 is outside the supplied excerpts. Lines 757-765 add a paragraph on streamed `auto` tool-call chunk framing: deltas share an `index`, the first carries id/type/name, and later ones carry argument fragments. Consumers concatenate the fragments. The paragraph describes behavior in libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMServer/Runtime/MLXOpenAIService.swift (`streamChatCompletionFrames`). The doc change adds no wire field, no authorization or attestation behavior, and no trust grant. It does not touch the E2E encryption contract: `inference_response_chunk` still carries `data` empty when encryption is active and `encrypted_data` otherwise (T-008). Tool-call fragments stay inside the encrypted SSE chunk payload.

The other changes in this PR are the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump (889fe3cc to f77b384c) and the remaining lines of the doc, which are unchanged context. I could not inspect the submodule diff, so the new streaming tool-call framing in MLXOpenAIService.swift and any other upstream change are unreviewed. Open questions for the next pass:
- Does the new streaming path keep tool-call fragments inside the encrypted chunk path and fail closed on encryption failure (T-008)?
- Does it add memory or DoS surface from unbounded argument buffering (T-010, T-029)?
- Does it leave the reserved tool-schema-metadata rejection and the prefix-cache, SSD and attestation code paths (T-041) unaffected?

A submodule bump with no visible diff is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety, so I am setting needs_deeper_review.
